history.dynasty: None documented (temple of the Bada Talab complex)
history.period: Talab: 1776 vs 1810-1815 (conflicting sources); temple later, renovated in modern times
history.summary: The Hanuman shrine on the eastern side of the Bada Talab (also called Rao Tej Singh Talab) in Rewari, opposite the Janana Ghat on the tank's western side. DATE CONFLICT: per the Haryana government website the tank was built by Rao Tej Singh during 1810-1815, but the municipal committee's inscription slab at the site says the work was completed in 1776. Per local documentation, the tank's Shiva temple came first, then the tank, with the Hanuman temple among later additions built to align with the original architecture. The Hanuman temple has been recently renovated with marble, vitrified tiles and granite; its garbhagriha faces north, it has two vimana towers, and the saffron-painted building is noted as distinct from all sides. NOTE: Google Maps reportedly marks the temple wrongly; look for the saffron building nearby. CSV town/state error: the CSV 'state' column holds the town name ('Rewari'); the correct state is Haryana.

town_description: Rewari is a historic city in southern Haryana and the administrative centre of Rewari district, about 80 km southwest of Delhi. An old Ahirwal trading town with a famous steam-locomotive shed museum, it is a major railway junction and a fast-growing NCR industrial hub.

travel.airport: Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi, about 90 km from Rewari.
travel.railway: Rewari Junction is the nearest major railway station.
travel.road: Hanuman Mandir Bada Talab, Kayasthwara Mohalla / Brass Market, Rewari 123401, on the eastern side of the Bada Talab.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Tuesdays and Saturdays are the busy worship days.
